name: One fail-loud setup script
claim_class: A claim that a deliverable's manual setup steps are ready for a human to run.
proof_obligation: When a deliverable needs a human to run steps in an environment the agent cannot reach, those steps ship as one script the human runs top to bottom, never as a prose checklist, because a checklist invites the wrong order, a skipped line, or a mistyped value, and setup steps get re-run often enough that paying for a script once is worth it. The script does everything that can be automated; it checks for anything that needs a human or an interactive installer instead of quietly installing it on its own, detecting what is missing and printing exactly what to install or set; it stops at the first real error and prints what broke, why, and what to do next, never swallowing an error to keep going, because in a bring-up script the errors are the point; it is safe to run more than once, skipping steps already done; and it reports precisely on exit, stating what was validated on success and printing the exact error on failure.
failure_mode: A prose checklist gets followed out of order, partially, or with a mistyped value nobody double-checked, and the resulting environment ends up subtly wrong in a way nobody catches until much later, because there was never a single script that could be re-run to confirm the setup was actually correct.
origin_incident: No single recorded event is documented for this rule. It generalizes a recurring pattern: manual setup instructions given as prose steps get run inconsistently, while a single script run the same way every time either works or fails loudly at the exact step that is wrong.
